title: Integral localization: monic inverse certificates and fraction comparison
statement:
Let $A,B$ be commutative integral domains, and let $\varphi:A\to B$ be an injective unital ring homomorphism. Assume $B$ is integral over $A$, meaning that every $b\in B$ satisfies a monic equation $b^n+\sum_{j<n}\varphi(a_j)b^j=0$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. Let $S=\varphi(A\setminus\{0\})$ and let $\iota:B\to C$ be a localization at $S$ [lem-weil-pbc-ring-localization-universal-property]: elements of $C$ are fractions $\iota(b)\iota(\varphi(a))^{-1}$ with $a\ne0$, and equality of fractions is equality after multiplying cross-products by some element of $S$.
For every nonzero $b\in B$ and every monic equation as above, write $a_n=1$ and let $i$ be the least index in $\{0,\ldots,n\}$ with $a_i\ne0$. Then $i<n$ and, for $d=\sum_{j=i+1}^n\varphi(a_j)b^{j-i-1}$, one has
$$\varphi(a_i)+bd=0,\qquad \iota(b)\bigl(-\iota(d)\iota(\varphi(a_i))^{-1}\bigr)=1.$$
Thus every nonzero element of $B$ has invertible image in $C$.
Let $L$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $j:B\to L$ an injective unital ring map making $L$ a field of fractions of $B$, meaning every $\ell\in L$ is $j(b)j(b')^{-1}$ with $b'\ne0$. The unique comparison $q:C\to L$ extending $j$ is bijective and satisfies
$$q\bigl(\iota(b)\iota(\varphi(a))^{-1}\bigr)=j(b)j(\varphi(a))^{-1}.$$
This holds for arbitrary integral extensions, without module finiteness or Noetherian hypotheses.

proof.text: Injectivity of $\varphi$ gives $\varphi(a_i)\ne0$, and $a_i\ne0$ puts this element in $S$. Its image in $C$ is therefore a unit. Apply $\iota$ to $bd=-\varphi(a_i)$ and multiply by $-\iota(\varphi(a_i))^{-1}$: $\iota(b)(-\iota(d)\iota(\varphi(a_i))^{-1})=1$. Commutativity gives the product in the reverse order too. For each nonzero $b$, integrality supplies such an equation, so this constructs an inverse for every $\iota(b)$.

source.place: Tag 00GS, lemma-integral-over-field (2), background only; explicit coefficient argument expanded by the agent; Tag 00CP, proposition-universal-property-localization, for the comparison map

proof.text: For $a\ne0$, injectivity of $\varphi$ and $j$ gives $j(\varphi(a))\ne0$. In the field $L$ it is a unit. Apply the localization universal property to $j:B\to L$ at $S$. It gives the unique ring map $q:C\to L$ extending $j$, with $q(\iota(b)\iota(\varphi(a))^{-1})=j(b)j(\varphi(a))^{-1}$.

source.place: Tag 00GS, lemma-integral-over-field (2), background only; explicit coefficient argument expanded by the agent; Tag 00CP, proposition-universal-property-localization, for the comparison map

proof.text: To prove injectivity, suppose $q(x)=q(y)$ and represent $x=\iota(u)\iota(\varphi(a))^{-1}$ and $y=\iota(v)\iota(\varphi(c))^{-1}$ with $a,c\ne0$. The formula for $q$ and multiplication by the nonzero denominators in $L$ give $j(u\varphi(c))=j(v\varphi(a))$. Injectivity of $j$ gives equality of these cross-products in $B$. The localization fraction equality criterion, taking the multiplier $1\in S$, now gives $x=y$.

source.place: Tag 00GS, lemma-integral-over-field (2), background only; explicit coefficient argument expanded by the agent; Tag 00CP, proposition-universal-property-localization, for the comparison map

proof.text: For surjectivity, write any $\ell\in L$ as $j(u)j(v)^{-1}$ with $v\ne0$. Step 2 supplies $w\in C$ with $\iota(v)w=1$. Applying $q$ gives $j(v)q(w)=1$; multiplying by $j(v)^{-1}$ gives $q(w)=j(v)^{-1}$. Thus $q(\iota(u)w)=\ell$. Together with step 4 this proves bijectivity. The argument used neither module finiteness nor a Noetherian hypothesis.
